title: God Sees the Truth, But Waits
text:
Ivan Aksionov, a cheerful young merchant of Vladimir, set out for the fair at Nizhny Novgorod although his wife had dreamed his hair had turned grey. At an inn on the way he shared a room with another merchant. Early in the morning he drove on, and later the police caught up with him. The other merchant had been found with his throat cut, and a bloody knife was in Aksionov's bag. He was flogged and sent to hard labor in Siberia.

He spent twenty-six years there. His hair turned white, he grew meek and prayed, and the other convicts respected him. Then a new prisoner arrived, Makar Semyonich, and from his talk Aksionov came to understand that this was the real murderer, who had planted the knife.

Soon after, Aksionov discovered Makar digging an escape tunnel under the bunks. When the guards found the tunnel, the governor questioned the prisoners, and Aksionov, who was known never to lie, was asked who had dug it. He could have destroyed Makar with one word. He said he would not tell.

That night Makar came to him in tears, confessed the murder, and begged forgiveness. Aksionov wept too, and said God would forgive him; perhaps he himself was a hundred times worse. At once his heart felt light. Makar confessed to the authorities. But when the order for Aksionov's release finally arrived, he was already dead.
lesson: Forgiving someone who has done you great wrong does not change the past, but it can free you from it. Do not wait for justice to make peace.
source: Leo Tolstoy, God Sees the Truth, But Waits (1872)
